newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Oil firms in Colombia must pay for security - Samper.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms in Colombia must pay for security - Samper.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper on Wednesday said foreign oil companies operating in his country must contribute to providing security for their operations.
"There are some programmes to improve (security) but those programmes must be paid for by the private sector," Samper told Reuters in an interview during an official visit to Israel.

Last week leftist rebels dynamited a section of Colombia's largest pipeline, halting operations. The pipeline carries about 220,000 barrels of crude a day from a field operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp. Last year rebels blew up the pipeline 47 times.
Samper said the private sector has already started to look out for its own security by flying drones over the pipelines and using private security systems.

"More than 30 percent of the army is involved in programmes to protect not only the oil fields but also pipelines, electrical towers and facilities. We are spending a lot of money to protect them," Samper said.
The president said there was also an effort to involve the local communities in protecting installations.
"Since we started with this programme the attempts to bomb the pipelines have been declining in a very important way," Samper said.
In an interview last month with the El Tiempo daily, Antonio Urdinola, head of state oil company Ecopetrol, said Colombia's security situation had worsened.
He warned that foreign investment in the oil sector could come to a standstill unless the government addresses security concerns of multinationals like Occidental or British Petroleum .

The head of Occidental's Colombian subsidiary told the same newspaper that 10 percent of the company's operating costs in Colombia went to security, not including a "war tax" of $17 million to the military this year.
